Sandbox_CeroSec_HardwareRequired_tooltip: On: a computer only reaches a door, window, lock or light that somebody has fitted a CeroSec module to -- a magnetic contact, a relay, an electric strike or a door operator, installed with a screwdriver and the Electricity skill. Off: every door, window, lock and light of the building is in /dev, wired or not, the way it was before this option existed.
Sandbox_CeroSec_PrefilledMachines_toolti: On: a computer switched on for the first time comes up with somebody's accounts on it, his files, a motd, a week of log and sometimes a password to find in a drawer nearby; a floppy off a shelf sometimes has a program and a README on it. Off: the bare machine -- two open accounts, an empty disk. A computer somebody has already switched on is never touched either way.
Sandbox_CeroSec_SafehouseModules_tooltip: On: a door, window, light, appliance or set standing inside a safehouse takes a CeroSec module -- and gives one back -- only for somebody that safehouse allows: its owner, its members, and an admin. Off, which is the default and the way it was before this option existed: the safehouse is no gate and anybody with the box, a screwdriver and the Electricity skill may wire it. No effect in single player. Looting rules are not consulted either way -- fitting a module is not looting.
Sandbox_CeroSec_ServerLog: Log the mod to the server console
Sandbox_CeroSec_ServerLog_tooltip: On: everything the mod says about itself is also printed to the game's console -- the server console on a dedicated server -- as "CeroSec: ..." lines, including every saved job dropped or refused at a load, every book that came back and how many of its jobs did, and every machine switched off for lack of power. Off, which is the default: the mod keeps those lines in memory only, and a dedicated server loses them at every restart. Safe to turn on for a bug hunt.
